newsitem.title: UK: GUS wants to expand direct mail in long term.
newsitem.headline: GUS wants to expand direct mail in long term.

text.p: Great Universal Stores Plc is looking at expanding it direct mail order business either via acquisition, franchising or by starting its own direct mail brand from scratch.

Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale, chairman of the home shopping and retailing group, said this might be a long term project for GUS to make use of its existing agency catalogue infrastructure to expand direct mail via niche or so-called "aspirational" branded catalogues. He said there were 10,000 small direct mail catalogues in the U.S. such as LL Bean and Eddie Bauer, and he expected this market to grow in the UK.
GUS's home shopping is almost entirely an agency business, relying on some 3.7 million agents to bring in orders and it only has a small direct mail business, Marshall Ward.
"We are looking at what is the route is to enter the small niche catalogue business," Wolfson told journalists, stressing this was not something GUS would do overnight.
He said one route would be to buy a niche player as Burton had done with Racing Green and Innovations, or do a franchise deal as Otto Versand had done with Eddie Bauer.
Wolfson blamed a fall in first half profits from home shopping on higher costs and a reduction in agent numbers.
He said the fall in agent numbers was part of plans to try to reduce agent "churn".
He said the company had spent three to five million stg in the first half on putting right problems with service levels, and would probably spend the same in the second half.
But the majority of the costs would be out of the way by the end of March 1997.

Wolfson also said changes to VAT payments relating to in-house credit proposed in last month's budget would cost the company about five million stg a year in profit terms and about seven million in terms of cash flow. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 7717
